cards.front: Angles on a straight line
cards.say: Angles on a straight line. Add up to one hundred and eighty degrees.

cards.front: Angles around a point
cards.say: Angles around a point. Add up to three hundred and sixty degrees.

cards.front: Angles in a triangle
cards.say: Angles in a triangle. Add up to one hundred and eighty degrees.

cards.front: Angles in a quadrilateral
cards.say: Angles in a quadrilateral. Add up to three hundred and sixty degrees.

cards.front: Vertically opposite angles
cards.back: Are equal. They are the pairs opposite each other where two straight lines cross.
cards.say: Vertically opposite angles. Are equal. They are the pairs opposite each other where two straight lines cross.

cards.front: Angles on a line: 50, 70 and x. Find x.
cards.say: Angles on a line: fifty, seventy and x. Find x. Sixty degrees. Fifty plus seventy equals one hundred and twenty, and one hundred and eighty minus one hundred and twenty equals sixty.

cards.front: Angles around a point: 90, 90, 120 and x. Find x.
cards.say: Angles around a point: ninety, ninety, one hundred and twenty and x. Find x. Sixty degrees. The three add to three hundred, and three hundred and sixty minus three hundred equals sixty.

cards.front: Triangle angles x, 2x and 3x. Find x.
cards.say: Triangle angles x, two x and three x. Find x. Thirty degrees. Six x equals one hundred and eighty, so x equals thirty. The angles are thirty, sixty, ninety.

cards.front: An isosceles triangle has a base angle of 50 degrees. Find the angle at the top.
cards.back: 80 degrees. The two base angles are 50 + 50 = 100, and 180 - 100 = 80.
cards.say: An isosceles triangle has a base angle of fifty degrees. Find the top angle. Eighty degrees. Two base angles make one hundred, and one hundred and eighty minus one hundred is eighty.

cards.front: Quadrilateral with angles 85, 95, 100 and x. Find x.
cards.say: A quadrilateral has angles eighty five, ninety five, one hundred and x. Find x. Eighty degrees, because the three add to two hundred and eighty, and three hundred and sixty minus that is eighty.

cards.front: Reflex angle on the other side of 110 degrees
cards.say: Reflex angle on the other side of one hundred and ten degrees. two hundred and fifty degrees. three hundred and sixty minus one hundred and ten equals two hundred and fifty.

figure.alt: An angle of 110 degrees drawn with two arms

cards.front: Angle between the clock hands at 3 o'clock
cards.back: 90 degrees. Each hour on a clock is 30 degrees, and 3 × 30 = 90.
cards.say: Angle between the clock hands at three o'clock. ninety degrees. Each hour on a clock is thirty degrees, and three times thirty equals ninety.

cards.front: Angle between the clock hands at 4 o'clock
cards.say: Angle between the clock hands at four o'clock. one hundred and twenty degrees. four times thirty equals one hundred and twenty.

cards.front: Angle between the clock hands at 6 o'clock
cards.back: 180 degrees. The hands make a straight line.
cards.say: Angle between the clock hands at six o'clock. one hundred and eighty degrees. The hands make a straight line.

cards.front: How many degrees does the hour hand move in one hour?
cards.say: How many degrees does the hour hand move in one hour? thirty degrees. three hundred and sixty divided by twelve equals thirty.

cards.front: Angles in a right-angled triangle: one is 90. The others add to...
cards.back: 90 degrees. The three add to 180, and 180 - 90 = 90.
cards.say: Angles in a right angled triangle: one is ninety. The others add to... ninety degrees. The three add to one hundred and eighty, and one hundred and eighty minus ninety equals ninety.

cards.front: Each angle in an equilateral triangle
cards.say: Each angle in an equilateral triangle. sixty degrees.

cards.front: Opposite angles of a parallelogram
cards.back: Are equal. The angles next to each other add up to 180 degrees.
cards.say: Opposite angles of a parallelogram. Are equal. The angles next to each other add up to one hundred and eighty degrees.

cards.front: Which turn is from facing north to facing south?
cards.say: Which turn is from facing north to facing south? A half turn, one hundred and eighty degrees.

cards.front: Which turn is from north clockwise to west?
cards.say: Which turn is from north clockwise to west? A three quarter turn, two hundred and seventy degrees.

cards.front: Angle types by size: acute, right, obtuse, straight, reflex. What is each?
cards.back: Acute: less than 90. Right: exactly 90. Obtuse: between 90 and 180. Straight: exactly 180. Reflex: between 180 and 360.
cards.say: Acute is less than ninety degrees. Right is exactly ninety. Obtuse is between ninety and one hundred and eighty. Straight is exactly one hundred and eighty. Reflex is more than one hundred and eighty.
